page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right, gathering signature at the foot.

p.i: nondum corruptum principatum exprimis, minus lu-xuriantem calamum restringo.

Bellorum formidandos in pace abortus, ne longius incremento proserpant, provida solertia à patriis limitibus amoliris. Nec sumptibus pro pace retinen-da, nec munificentia pro dignitate parcis. Nunquam prudentiam casui, nec judicium temeritati committis. Convenientem imperantis majestati venusta-tem, laboriosò corporis exercitio fovendam, non asper-naris.

Imperii tui vires, nec minus vires hostium, & fœ-dera offerentium cum voluntate facultates, maturè metiris. Curarum radios, non uno loci situ concludendos, ad multa simul dispergis. Infecundarum fluxu alteram fortunam, tanquam præsentem, contempla-ris. Luxum, intima reip. viscera corrosurum, legum severitate comprimis. Ærarium inanibus in hi-strionias delusiones erogationibus, & pudendis pota-tionum certaminibus, minus, pro more seculi, exhau-ris. Rebus in aula, in curia, in militia administran-dis capaces rerum viros præficis. Nec paupertatem ignominia, nec opulentiam subditorum incutienda formidine [?]sectaris.

Fanis religioso cultui dicatis, & honestarum ar-tium officinis lycéis, aperiendis incrementa & fum-ptus porrigis. Inconcussam, domi & foris, pacem bel-li triumpho gloriosiorem ducis. Serenitate vultus & sermonis, opportuna severitate interveniente, cum gravitate venerationem retines. Nec promiscuam

page.notes: Text is set in italic throughout; the whole body is italicised, so paragraphs are wrapped in one <i> each. The word in the third paragraph read as "[?]sectaris" is uncertain: the letters are unclear and could be "fectaris" or "sectaris". A small mark above the running head at top centre is a printer's mark and was not transcribed. Faint show-through from the reverse side appears in the right and left margins and was ignored. The paragraph ending "Nec promiscuam" continues onto the following page.
